subject: Renewal proposal — priority support uplift & latency guardrails
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@silverline.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@silverline.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal — priority support uplift & latency guardrails

Hi Olivia / Samir,

Thanks again for the productive renewal conversation last week. Per our call, I pulled together a compact proposal that moves Silverline from the standard support tier to our Priority Support offering at renewal, and includes a new latency SLO band targeted at 95th percentile tail latency for inference traffic.

Key points in this email:
- Priority Support: 24/7 priority routing to operations + a dedicated escalation path (phone pager and Slack bridge), monthly NFR credits for burst incidents.
- Latency SLOs: target 95th percentile <= 150ms for your production model profiles, with a measured baseline period and a 60-day onramp for caching/batching tuning.
- Commitment: 12-month term with a 20% uplift on committed capacity; can add a burst buffer for sudden seasonal spikes.

I've attached a short PDF that lists the exact response SLA, onboarding milestones, and the proposed price ladder. If this matches the direction you want, we can create the formal amendment and include Marcus and Aditya from my side for any legal/finance approvals.

Request: Could you confirm whether the 12-month term is fine and whether you want the burst buffer enabled at sign? If yes, I'll surface pricing and a mutually agreeable rollout schedule.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — priority support uplift & latency guardrails

Hi Soojin,

Thanks — appreciate the summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we move to contract:
1) The 95th pct <=150ms sounds reasonable for inference traffic to our production model (avg seq 128), but what happens if we miss the SLO during peak campaigns?
2) Burst buffer: we prefer to start without the buffer for the first quarter unless we see clear evidence of traffic spikes.
3) Pricing: can you show the delta vs our current spend and the recommended tradeoffs (eg. quantization + caching vs higher committed capacity)?

If you can send an updated amendment with those clarifications, we can scope review with our procurement and infra leads. CC'ing Samir who will own procurement.

Best,
Olivia
VP Product, Silverline AI
olivia@silverline.ai

Thanks for the context. Short answers:
- Legal/ops stance: we can include a standard service credit ladder for missed SLOs (credits scaled to incident severity and duration), plus a 4-week remediation window where we jointly execute performance tuning before credits escalate. That should satisfy procurement in most cases. We'll avoid hard monetary SLAs beyond credits unless they push.
- During the onramp tuning period: we explicitly mark a 60-day performance stabilization window in the amendment where SLOs are 'measured but not credit-bearing' aside from severe outages. That gives our team and theirs time to optimize caching/batching and KV cache priming.
- Pricing delta: Aditya, can you sketch the two options Soojin requested and attach a worksheet?

I'll draft a short amendment paragraph for the exceptions and the onramp language.

—Marcus

Attached is a short worksheet (see Latency_SLO_Appendix.xlsx) with current monthly spend, delta for a 20% committed uplift, and an alternate option that pairs a 10% uplift with a one-time Ops Advisory (flat fee). Quick summary:
- Option A (20% uplift + Priority Support): ~+21% ARR vs current committed spend, includes 24/7 priority routing and 2x monthly NFR credits.
- Option B (10% uplift + Ops Advisory): ~+9% ARR plus a one-time $15k Ops Advisory engagement to tune caching, batching, and quantization recommendations. Expected to hit target SLO in 30–45 days if they follow the advisory playbook.

Recommendation: propose Option B as the recommended path (lower near-term cost and a focused ops uplift). If they opt for Option A, add an optional trial burst buffer that can be toggled after the first quarter.

I'll convert this into the amendment language and pricing table once you confirm which option to present.

Hi Olivia / Samir —

Thanks for the quick review. Based on internal alignment, here are the revised, actionable options for Silverline's renewal. I've attached the updated PDF amendment with the SLO onramp language and the pricing worksheet.

Option 1 — Priority Support + 10% uplift + Ops Advisory (recommended)
- Term: 12 months
- Capacity uplift: 10% committed
- One-time Ops Advisory: $15,000 (30–45 day engagement to tune caching/batching/quantization and run a post-tune validation)
- SLO: 95th pct <=150ms measured after 60-day stabilization window; credits only for severe outages during stabilization.

Option 2 — Priority Support + 20% uplift (simpler)
- Term: 12 months
- Capacity uplift: 20% committed
- Burst buffer: optional post-sign (add-on)
- SLO: 95th pct <=150ms after 60-day stabilization; standard credit ladder applies.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm preferred option and whether Procurement wants Option A or B on the table.
2) On confirmation, we convert the attached PDF into an official amendment for signature (we can do DocuSign).
3) If Option 1 is chosen, we schedule the Ops Advisory kickoff with Marcus and the CS runbook.

Let me know if you want a short call tomorrow to walk through the worksheet. If we can get consent by next Wednesday, we can include the amendment in the 10/15 renewal cycle.

Best —
